brief.headline: Mariana has lost 8% of her body weight (77.9 to 71.7 kg) from Sep 5 to Nov 24, 2026, with poor appetite. Her son and primary caregiver also reported exhaustion and asked for respite on Sep 27.

items.statement: Weight fell 6.2 kg (13.7 lb, 8.0%) from 77.9 kg on 2026-09-05 to 71.7 kg on 2026-11-24. The decline was steady across readings: 75.7 kg on 10/01 and 73.6 kg on 10/28. The dietitian documented poor appetite, skipped breakfast, and about 50% of day center lunches eaten.
items.verifier_note: Weights, change (-6.2 kg, -13.7 lb, -8.0%) and intermediate readings match the vitals record. The dietitian note supports poor appetite, skipped breakfast and about 50% of lunches eaten.

items.statement: On 2026-09-27 her son Marcus, the primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He worries about managing evenings alone and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed. The notes do not show any follow-up or outcome.
items.verifier_note: The social work note supports the exhaustion, poor sleep, evening worries, respite request and the discussion of options and a support group. The cited note shows no follow-up, which matches the statement.

items.statement: The dietitian's 2026-11-24 plan includes an oral nutrition supplement twice daily, weekly weights, and a dental check for chewing problems. The record shows no medication starts in the period, and no dental appointment is documented.
items.verifier_note: The plan items match the dietitian note. The medication record shows no starts or stops. The cited sources document no dental appointment.

items.statement: PCP progress notes on 2026-09-02, 09-27 and 11-27 describe chronic conditions as stable with the current plan continued. The 11-27 note, written three days after the 8% weight loss was documented, does not mention it.
items.verifier_note: All three PCP notes say chronic conditions are stable and the plan continues. The 11-27 note does not mention weight loss, and it falls three days after the 11-24 dietitian note.

items.statement: Blood pressure readings on 9/13, 10/14 and 11/12 were 130/74, 134/77 and 130/72. None met the 140/90 elevated threshold. No encounters (ED or hospital) were recorded in the period.
items.verifier_note: The BP values and dates match the vitals record, elevated_count is 0 against the 140/90 threshold, and the encounters record is empty.

questions_for_team: What could be driving the poor appetite and weight loss, and does anyone need to review it beyond the dietitian's plan?
Who is following up on Marcus's respite request from 9/27, and what support is in place for his evenings?
Is the oral supplement started, and who is recording the weekly weights?
Has the dental check been scheduled?
Does the PCP need to be told about the weight trend, given the 11/27 note says stable?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and that the participant's data covers the full period since the last IDT review; note any gaps in charting.
Falls and near-falls: count and circumstances in the window, with injury assessment. Relevant given osteoporosis, beta-blocker use, and nitroglycerin use.
ED visits and hospital admissions in the window: reason, discharge plan, and any follow-up appointments that were missed or still pending.

Cardiac symptoms: chest pain or angina episodes, nitroglycerin use frequency (active PRN spray), dyspnea, palpitations, edema, and any new cardiology visits. Ischemic heart disease and hypertension are on the problem list.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend across the window, including orthostatic readings if recorded, given metoprolol succinate and essential hypertension.

Medication changes: review the active list (metoprolol succinate 100 mg, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin 20 mg, vitamin B12 injections) for any starts, stops, or dose changes in the window, and confirm who prescribed them. Check whether the statin is still the intended intensity given ischemic heart disease and diabetes, as a question for the prescriber rather than a recommendation.

Glycemic and renal monitoring: most recent HbA1c, fasting or random glucose trend, and whether a diabetes medication is recorded. The active list has no glucose-lowering agent despite type 2 diabetes, so confirm whether this is intentional. Check eGFR and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio given CKD stage 1 due to diabetes, and the trend of any renal labs.

Anemia and B12 follow-up: latest hemoglobin and CBC, iron or B12 levels, and whether B12 injection doses are on schedule and documented as given. Confirm the injection schedule and who administers it.
Weight and BMI trend: compare current weight with prior values, given obesity (BMI 30+), diabetes, and hypertriglyceridemia. Check lipid panel (triglycerides, LDL) for recency.

Function and ADLs/IADLs: changes in bathing, dressing, toileting, transfers, medication management, meal preparation, and transportation since last review, plus any new assistive devices or home services.

Cognition, mood and social: screen results or observed changes in memory, confusion, depressed mood, or isolation; attendance at PACE day programs, transportation reliability, and missed appointments; caregiver or family situation changes and caregiver strain; care-plan items due in the window (reassessments, goal reviews, osteoporosis treatment and bone density follow-up, eye and foot exams for diabetes) with status flagged.
